introduction.definition: An air-cooled heat exchanger (fin-fan) cools or condenses a process stream with ambient air. The fluid flows through finned tubes between header boxes; axial fans force air across the bundle. It removes the need for cooling water.

classification.type: Forced draft, plug-type headers, two fans

introduction.summary: An air-cooled heat exchanger (fin-fan cooler) cools or condenses a process fluid using ambient air instead of water. The fluid flows through finned tubes between header boxes; axial fans blow (forced draft) or pull (induced draft) air across the bundle. It saves cooling water and is common in refineries and gas plants.

foundation: Elevate on structure with free air inlet; avoid hot-air recirculation and nearby obstructions.
alignment: Provide pull-out space for tube bundles or plates; align nozzles to piping without strain.
piping: Install vents and drains on both sides; fit strainers where fouling solids are expected.
commissioning: Pressure-test each side; vent air; bring flows on gradually to avoid thermal shock.

video_tutorials.title: Air Cooled Heat Exchanger — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Air Cooled Heat Exchanger.
An air-cooled heat exchanger (fin-fan) cools or condenses a process stream with ambient air.
The fluid flows through finned tubes between header boxes; axial fans force air across the bundle.
It removes the need for cooling water.
Typical applications include refinery and gas-plant product coolers and condensers; compressor inter/after-coolers; power-plant air-cooled condensers; remote sites without water.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Fan Plenum & Fan Rings, Axial Fan 1 (adjustable-pitch blades), Axial Fan 2 (adjustable-pitch blades).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Air Cooled Heat Exchanger works.
Hot fluid enters the inlet header and is spread over the tubes.
Fans push ambient air up through the finned bundle.
Heat passes from the fluid through the tube and fins into the air.
Cooled fluid leaves through the outlet header nozzle.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Air Cooled Heat Exchanger — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Air Cooled Heat Exchanger.
Check fan vibration and belt/drive.
Wash fins (low-pressure water).
Check fan pitch and tip clearance.
Remove plugs; clean and inspect tubes.
Watch for fin fouling: high outlet temperature. Common cause: dust, insects, fibres.
Watch for fan failure: loss of capacity, vibration. Common cause: bearing/belt failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
